newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia bank confirms security issue on 8.5 pct UES.
newsitem.headline: Russia bank confirms security issue on 8.5 pct UES.

text.p: Russia's National Reserve Bank (Natsionalny Rezervny Bank in Russian) is working with power utility UES on a plan to issue securities on an 8.5 percent stake in the company it owns as part of a wider consortium, a bank spokesman said on Monday.

"We are working in that direction with RAO UES, but no one is ready to put that programme on the table yet. But we can say that we'll come up with something in 1997," Alexander Drozdov, personal adviser to the chairman of NRB, told Reuters.

United Energy System (UES) president Anatoly Dyakov said earlier that the consortium of banks, which bought a 8.5 percent stake in January, was planning to issue securities -- most likely convertible bonds -- on the shares.
He also said UES could receive one trillion roubles to invest in new power stations from the issue.

But Drozdov said the type of securities to be issued had not yet been determined, although convertible bonds were among the possibilities under consideration, and that discussions about one trillion roubles to be given to UES were ongoing.
He did not say whether UES would receive the money as a credit or whether it would be under other terms.
"Up to now we haven't been eager to give credits to industry, where non-payment has become a normal practice, but RAO UES is a significant exception," Drozdov said.
He suggested that much would depend on reforms at UES.
"It's very important to hear from the government and from First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov exactly what they have in mind when they talk about restructuring UES," Drozdov said.
A consortium of banks headed by Natsionalny Rezervny Bank bought the 8.5 percent share in UES at a special auction earlier this year.
